description: A doctoral research seminar on why learning algorithms generalise: PAC and VC theory, Rademacher and PAC-Bayes bounds, online learning, boosting, active and semi-supervised learning, differential privacy and over-parameterised models. Students prove core results, test bounds numerically against simulated learners, critique recent papers and write a research proposal on an open problem.
modelledOn: Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
Mohri, Rostamizadeh and Talwalkar, Foundations of Machine Learning
Dwork and Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
outcomes: Prove sample-complexity and generalisation bounds using concentration inequalities, VC dimension and Rademacher complexity.
Analyse online learning algorithms through regret and mistake bounds, and relate online guarantees to statistical ones.
Explain boosting, active learning and semi-supervised learning through margin and label-complexity arguments.
Design and analyse differentially private learning mechanisms and quantify the accuracy cost of privacy.
Critique recent theoretical work on over-parameterised models, identifying which assumptions and bounds do and do not explain observed behaviour.
Formulate an open problem and write a research proposal with a precise question, related work, approach and evaluation plan.

units.title: The learning problem and concentration
topics: Empirical risk minimisation, true risk, hypothesis classes and the realisable and agnostic settings
No-free-lunch theorem and the approximation-estimation trade-off
Concentration inequalities: Hoeffding, Bernstein and McDiarmid bounded differences
Uniform convergence for finite classes by the union bound
Surrogate losses and classification calibration
Bayes-optimal predictors and statistical consistency

units.title: PAC learning and VC theory
topics: PAC and agnostic PAC learning; sample complexity definitions
Growth function, Sauer-Shelah lemma and VC dimension
Fundamental theorem of statistical learning: equivalence of learnability, uniform convergence and finite VC dimension
VC dimension of halfspaces, polynomial thresholds and neural networks
Lower bounds on sample complexity and the no-free-lunch argument
Computational complexity of learning: proper versus improper learning and hardness results

units.title: Rademacher complexity and generalisation bounds
topics: Rademacher complexity, symmetrisation and generalisation bounds
Contraction lemma and bounds for linear classes with norm constraints
Margin bounds for support vector machines and kernel methods
Covering numbers, Dudley's entropy integral and chaining
Algorithmic stability and generalisation of regularised ERM
PAC-Bayes bounds and their use for non-vacuous bounds on learned models
Data-dependent and local complexity bounds; fast rates

units.title: Online learning and regret
topics: The online protocol; mistake bounds, the Halving algorithm and Littlestone dimension
Perceptron mistake bound and online-to-batch conversion
Experts, weighted majority and Hedge
Online convex optimisation: online gradient descent and regret of order square root of T
Multi-armed and contextual bandits: UCB and EXP3
Adversarial versus stochastic settings; best-of-both-worlds algorithms

units.title: Boosting and margin theory
topics: Weak learnability and the boosting question
AdaBoost: algorithm, training-error bound and the role of weak-learner edge
Margin explanation of generalisation and its criticisms
Boosting as coordinate descent and functional gradient descent; relation to support vector machines
Boosting under noise: convex and non-convex losses and robustness

units.title: Active, semi-supervised and transfer learning theory
topics: Active learning: label complexity, disagreement coefficient and exponential savings
Query by committee and margin-based active learning
Semi-supervised learning: cluster and manifold assumptions, and when unlabelled data provably helps
Co-training and multi-view learning
Domain adaptation: discrepancy distances and generalisation bounds under shift
Learning with few labels in low-resource settings: transfer, weak supervision and what theory says about it

units.title: Differential privacy
topics: Definition of pure and approximate differential privacy; post-processing and group privacy
Laplace, Gaussian and exponential mechanisms
Composition: basic and advanced composition, and privacy accounting
Private empirical risk minimisation and DP-SGD; the sample-complexity cost of privacy
Privacy and generalisation: adaptive data analysis and the reusable holdout
Privacy for health and mobile data: local differential privacy and federated analytics

units.title: Theory of over-parameterised models
topics: Classical bias-variance versus double descent; interpolation and the failure of classical bounds
Benign overfitting in linear regression and minimum-norm interpolation
Implicit bias of gradient descent: convergence to the maximum-margin solution
Neural tangent kernel, lazy training and the limits of the kernel regime
Feature learning and mean-field analysis of two-layer networks
PAC-Bayes and compression-based bounds for deep networks
Limits of uniform convergence and stability explanations; open debates

units.title: Research frontiers and proposal
topics: Reading a theory paper critically: assumptions, constants, tightness and empirical relevance
Scaling behaviour of generalisation and sample complexity in modern learning systems
Robust learning, calibration and uncertainty: theoretical guarantees and gaps
Open problems in the course and ways to formulate them as precise questions
Proposal workshop: structure, related work, preliminary results and evaluation plan

schedule.title: The learning problem, concentration and finite classes
schedule.exercise: Prove the finite-class generalisation bound using Hoeffding and the union bound, then discuss in a one-page note why no learner is universally best and how surrogate losses relate to the 0-1 loss.

tasks.title: Estimate by simulation how often an empirical mean of bounded variables deviates by more than epsilon, and compare with the Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds
Run ERM on a finite class of 50 thresholds for training sizes 10 to 1000, and plot the generalisation gap against the finite-class bound
Compare the 0-1, hinge, logistic and exponential losses as functions of margin, and check classification calibration numerically for each

schedule.title: PAC learning and VC dimension
schedule.exercise: Show that intervals on the line have VC dimension 2, derive the growth function bound, and sketch the proof that finite VC dimension implies uniform convergence.

tasks.title: Compute the growth function for thresholds and intervals on the line for sample sizes 1 to 10, and compare it with the Sauer-Shelah bound
Shatter-test axis-aligned rectangles in the plane by brute force on 3, 4 and 5 points and confirm the VC dimension is 4
Compute the sample size from the VC bound for target error 0.05 and confidence 0.95 across VC dimensions 5 to 50, and plot how it scales

schedule.title: VC dimension of common classes and lower bounds
schedule.exercise: Prove that halfspaces in d dimensions have VC dimension d + 1, discuss a lower-bound argument, and critique a paper on the hardness of improper learning.

tasks.title: Verify that halfspaces in the plane shatter 3 points but not 4 by enumerating labelings and testing linear separability of each
Construct a hard distribution for a class with VC dimension d, estimate the error of ERM across sample sizes, and show the lower-bound rate
Review a recent hardness-of-learning paper in a seminar case file, identify its assumptions, and judge what it implies for practical learners

schedule.title: Rademacher complexity and linear classes
schedule.exercise: Prove the Rademacher bound via symmetrisation, derive the complexity of norm-bounded linear classes, and compare the resulting margin bound with the VC bound.

tasks.title: Estimate the empirical Rademacher complexity of a class of thresholds and a class of linear predictors by Monte Carlo with 2000 sign draws
Compute the Rademacher bound for linear classes with bounded weight norm for various data radii, and plot it against sample size
Train a support vector machine on 5 datasets, compute the margin bound, and compare it with the observed test error in a table

schedule.title: Chaining, stability and PAC-Bayes
schedule.exercise: Compare uniform-convergence, stability and PAC-Bayes explanations of generalisation, and evaluate whether a published bound for a trained network is non-vacuous.

tasks.title: Measure the leave-one-out stability of ridge regression as the regulariser varies, and compare the gap to the stability bound
Compute a PAC-Bayes bound for a Gaussian posterior around a trained linear classifier and tune the prior variance to tighten it
Critique a paper claiming a tight bound for deep networks in a seminar case file, listing assumptions, constants and where the bound could break

schedule.title: Online learning and regret
schedule.exercise: Prove the regret bound of Hedge and online gradient descent, convert an online learner into a batch learner, and compare UCB and EXP3 on stochastic and adversarial bandit instances.

tasks.title: Run Hedge against experts with different loss patterns, plot regret against T, and compare it with the square-root bound
Compute online gradient descent regret on a convex loss sequence for several step sizes, and find the step size that minimises the bound
Compare UCB and EXP3 on a stochastic bandit and on an adversarial schedule, plotting cumulative regret over 10,000 rounds for each

schedule.title: Boosting and margins
schedule.exercise: Prove the AdaBoost training-error bound, discuss the margin explanation of its resistance to overfitting and the objections to it, and relate boosting to coordinate descent on exponential loss.

tasks.title: Step through five rounds of AdaBoost with decision stumps, showing sample weights, weak-learner error and the combined classifier each round
Run AdaBoost for 500 rounds, plot training error, test error and the margin distribution, and relate changes in margins to test error
Add label noise of 5 and 20 percent to a dataset, compare AdaBoost with logistic-loss boosting, and explain the difference in robustness

schedule.title: Active and semi-supervised learning
schedule.exercise: Show an exponential label saving for active learning of thresholds, then state the assumptions under which unlabelled data provably helps and give a counterexample.

tasks.title: Compare active learning of a threshold by binary search with passive learning, and plot label count against target error
Implement margin-based active learning for linear separators on 2D data, and compare labels needed with random sampling
Compare a supervised classifier with a cluster-assumption semi-supervised one on two datasets, one satisfying the assumption and one violating it

schedule.title: Domain adaptation and learning with few labels
schedule.exercise: Derive a domain-adaptation bound with a discrepancy term, and write a critique of a paper that claims transfer learning helps in a low-resource African language setting.

tasks.title: Estimate the discrepancy between source and target distributions on a simulated shift, and compare it with the target-error increase of a trained classifier
Train a classifier on a source distribution, evaluate it on shifted targets, and test whether importance weighting reduces the gap
Evaluate in a seminar case file a weak-supervision approach for a low-resource language, deciding what theory can promise and what it cannot

schedule.title: Differential privacy
schedule.exercise: Prove that the Laplace mechanism satisfies epsilon-differential privacy, compose three queries under basic and advanced composition, and analyse the accuracy cost of DP-SGD.

tasks.title: Apply the Laplace mechanism to a counting query across epsilon values 0.1 to 5, and plot expected error against the privacy budget
Compute total privacy loss after 100 queries under basic and advanced composition and find when advanced composition gives a tighter bound
Train a classifier with DP-SGD using clipping and noise, and plot test accuracy against epsilon on a health-style dataset

schedule.title: Classical and modern generalisation
schedule.exercise: Reproduce the double-descent curve in a random-features regression, explain benign overfitting for minimum-norm interpolation, and show gradient descent finds the maximum-margin separator.

tasks.title: Fit random-features regression for feature counts from 10 to 500 on 100 samples and plot test error to reveal double descent
Run gradient descent on logistic loss on separable data, track the direction of the weights, and show it converges to the max-margin direction
Compute the neural tangent kernel of a small two-layer network at initialisation and compare kernel regression with the trained network

schedule.title: Feature learning, deep-network bounds and open debates
schedule.exercise: Compare feature-learning and kernel regimes for a two-layer network, discuss why uniform convergence may fail for deep models, and prepare a paper-critique seminar presentation.

tasks.title: Train a two-layer network at large and small width, and compare how far the hidden features move from initialisation in each regime
Compute a compression-based or PAC-Bayes bound for a trained small network, and report whether it is non-vacuous against the observed error
Present and defend a critique of a recent paper on generalisation of deep networks in a seminar case file against the rubric

schedule.title: Open problems and proposal workshop
schedule.exercise: Choose an open problem from the course, write a two-page research proposal with a precise question, related work, approach, preliminary experiment and evaluation plan, and present it for review.

tasks.title: Review a theory paper for a mock conference in a case file, assessing assumptions, constants and tightness, and recommend accept or reject
Run a small experiment testing whether a published guarantee on calibration or robustness holds on a simulated task, and report the gap
Plot a preliminary result from your proposal, such as a bound versus empirical curve, and write the caption and claim it supports
